parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or adult care in the division; no statewide adult facility ban; marriage and private intimacy lawful. Against that, the national entry regime treats marker/presentation discrepancy as possible wilful misrepresentation, with refusal, secondary screening, case-note tagging and potential lifetime fraud ineligibility; federally funded single-sex facility exclusion is a universal exposure; immigration custody harm is documented; and the division supplies no state-level nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage outside four municipalities, so service denial has thin local recourse. National courts have enjoined some orders and the passport rule is still litigated, so the operative picture is contested and journalled by advisories from allied governments.

entry_documents.exposure: National marker policy bars self-selected sex on passports/visas; officers must refuse cases where records cast doubt on sex, may consider a permanent, lifetime fraud ineligibility finding, and add a case-note tag; trans athletes barred; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports stay valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist; the policy is under national civil-liberties litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport marker meets national screening, visa adjudication and airline verification; a discrepancy can escalate from secondary inspection to refusal and a fraud record, while the division's own marker rules never touch the visitor's documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: In immigration custody trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections policy imposes hair-cutting, hormone withdrawal and psychiatric substitution on trans inmates, and prisoner counts stopped being reported in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Several executive orders have been enjoined, but no facility-level safeguard for detained trans visitors is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document or misrepresentation query at the border converts a traveller into a detainee, where the documented custodial practices, not the street-level climate, govern the outcome.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities matching identity; four states criminalise bathroom use in some circumstances and one student was handcuffed and held in a men's ward; this division bans trans girls from school sports and one district routes trans students to birth-sex or nurse's facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No statewide adult restroom/changing-room ban in the division; four municipal ordinances (about 46% of population) cover public accommodations; the district policy is school-only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Adult visitors face exposure mainly in national buildings and federally funded settings; division-level adult facilities carry no statutory bar, though district precedent signals local hostility.

care_services.exposure: The division's appointed medical board approved a draft rule making gender-transition care for under-18s unprofessional conduct; national orders frame minors' care as mutilation and propose barring public insurance reimbursement under 18.
care_services.protection: Adult gender-affirming care is lawful with no statewide ban; the draft rule still requires law-department review and a 30-day comment period before operating; injunctions have blocked several national orders.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitors can seek care; a family travelling with a trans minor may meet provider refusal driven by disciplinary risk even though no final rule binds yet.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; a 2025 justice memorandum lists 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist animating views; an order directs investigation of schools facilitating a minor's social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined several orders; the reward memorandum never uses gender ideology as a criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises the odds that advocacy, online content or school contact draws official attention, but it does not itself criminalise transgender status or presentation for a visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: An executive order invites criminal prosecution of teachers using a trans minor's name or pronouns; the division bars trans girls from girls' sports and one district forces birth-sex facilities or the nurse's office; a pending board rule threatens clinicians treating under-18s.
minors_guardians.protection: The board rule is not operative; the sports and facilities measures are school-scoped and do not bind adult visitors; no provision penalises a parent travelling with a trans child as such.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family's exposure runs through schools, athletics and clinicians rather than police; a guardian enrolling a minor locally inherits the district and board rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The division's hate-crime statute omits gender identity, so bias violence draws no state enhancement; no trans-specific violence count or homicide baseline is recorded; polling shows 66% backing birth-sex document rules and 69% backing birth-sex sport rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; four municipal ordinances prohibit discrimination; no documented pattern of police targeting or trans killings in the division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor assaulted or refused service outside the four municipalities has no state enhancement or accommodation remedy and must rely on national or municipal avenues of unverified reach.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination coverage means hotels, restaurants and employers outside four cities face no state sanction; enforcement of even those ordinances is unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active national litigation against the passport rule, a legal-aid FAQ on document rules, and courts willing to enjoin executive orders; the division allows document changes, though with a retained former-name notation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists mainly at national level and moves slowly against a screening regime applied at the moment of entry, which is the traveller's least remediable stage.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia arrests and imprisons on presentation with compelled confessions and a latent capital clause. Here nothing criminalises transgender status or presentation, custody abuse occurs in immigration detention rather than as routine sentence after discovery, and courts enjoin hostile orders — materially above this floor.

Vellandra denies entry through an unpublished morality register with no remedy. This regime's entry machinery is comparable in traveller-facing exposure (discretionary refusal, tagging, lifetime ineligibility), but adds documented custodial harm and facility exclusion in national buildings, so it sits above the pure exclusion tier yet below any jurisdiction with working review.

Kestrel Isles secondary screening, discretionary refusal and humiliating searches resemble this border tier, but its penalties stay administrative and reversible on appeal. Here a refusal can seed a permanent fraud finding and allied governments issued advisories, making consequence-severity higher than this anchor.

Meridia pairs document flexibility for trans travellers with tribunal review and release after brief detention. Here adjudicators must refuse discrepant cases and detention exposes documented abuse, so the traveller-facing entry and custody position is clearly worse than this anchor.

Brindlewick requires enforceable equality notices on carriers, trained transit police and prompt independent review. This regime instead directs refusal for document doubt, omits state-level public-accommodations coverage in most of the division, and leaves national-level litigation unresolved — far below.

parsed.synthesis: The division's own statutes are comparatively light for an adult visitor: no adult restroom ban, no adult care ban, marriage and intimacy lawful. Risk comes from the national layer operating through the journey. Documents are the pivot: a passport marker or presentation mismatch invites refusal, a case-note tag and potentially a lifetime fraud finding, and flight or detention puts the traveller inside a Custody system with documented forced labour, hormone withdrawal and sexual abuse. Facility exclusion in federally funded buildings is universal exposure, not discretionary. Local recourse is thin outside four municipalities, and the hate-crime gap leaves violence unenhanced, mitigated only by a national statute and unfinished litigation.
